subsystems.name: Accelerator
subsystems.role: does the matrix arithmetic that dominates language-model inference.

subsystems.name: Host processor and memory
subsystems.role: runs the operating system and moves weights and activations into the accelerator.

subsystems.name: Storage
subsystems.role: holds model weights, which run to tens or hundreds of gigabytes.

subsystems.name: Inference runtime
subsystems.role: turns a stored model into tokens, as fast as the hardware allows.

subsystems.name: Thermal and power system
subsystems.role: keeps a machine that runs hot and continuously quiet enough for a home.
parts: heatsink and fans or liquid loop

subsystems.name: Local service boundary
subsystems.role: exposes the model to apps on the home network without sending data off it.

buildSteps.title: Fix the model budget
buildSteps.detail: Decide which model sizes and context lengths the box must serve, since they set the hard memory floor: a 4-bit quantised model needs roughly half a gigabyte of memory per billion parameters, plus cache.

buildSteps.title: Pick the memory architecture
buildSteps.detail: Inference is usually memory-bandwidth-bound, not compute-bound, so the design starts by choosing on-package memory delivering hundreds of gigabytes to a few terabytes per second.

buildSteps.title: Design or select the accelerator
buildSteps.detail: Specify integer matrix-multiply units and cache sized for quantised weights, with an instruction set the compiler can target.

buildSteps.title: Assemble board and package
buildSteps.detail: Accelerator die, memory stacks and host components are packaged together and mounted on a board with a small firmware image for boot and power management.

buildSteps.title: Bring up firmware and drivers
buildSteps.detail: Boot the board, load the accelerator driver, and validate that memory errors and thermal throttling are detected and handled.

buildSteps.title: Build the inference kernels
buildSteps.detail: Write and tune routines for 4-bit and 8-bit weights: dequantise, multiply, accumulate, and keep the arithmetic units fed from cache rather than from main memory.

buildSteps.title: Integrate model management
buildSteps.detail: Add download of open-weight models, conversion and calibration into quantised formats, and an LRU cache so switching models does not stall.

buildSteps.title: Tune acoustics and thermals
buildSteps.detail: Set fan curves and power caps so sustained generation does not sound like a rack server in a living room.

buildSteps.title: Validate and ship
buildSteps.detail: Measure time-to-first-token, tokens per second, memory ceiling and wall power, then ship with a local API and documented privacy guarantees.

prerequisites.why: 4-bit and 8-bit schemes such as GGUF, GPTQ and AWQ are how large models fit in consumer memory at all.
HBM and LPDDR5X exist, but the cheapest large-bandwidth parts are still costly and supply-constrained.
accelerators are shipping in laptops and small boards, but vendor compilers and operator coverage lag what the inference runtimes need.
grouped-query attention and sparse experts cut cost per token, but the KV cache still grows with context length.
without downloadable weights there is nothing to run locally.

pathway.milestone: local inference on workstations, gaming GPUs and unified-memory desktops using open runtimes
pathway.unlocks: private, offline assistants for enthusiasts and small offices.

pathway.milestone: quiet, fanless-or-near-silent appliances with 64–256 GB of fast memory at a few hundred watts
pathway.unlocks: a home box that serves a mid-size model to every device in the house.

pathway.milestone: open NPU toolchains and standard quantised kernels across vendors
pathway.unlocks: portable software, so models are not locked to one accelerator.

pathway.milestone: on-device fine-tuning and personal retrieval indexes
pathway.unlocks: assistants tuned to one household's data without that data ever leaving it.
